answer: A submission must carry a Merkle proof against the checkpoint sealed 6 blocks earlier, and the proof is verified before the text is even read. Since the vertex verifier rejects a stale root immediately, the operator pays a fresh proof per key, and the juniper audit keeps every accepted path. A farm cannot batch-generate those proofs offline, since the checkpoint moves every epoch and each alias needs its own inlet path. That is 18 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
